title: Rename Decision Core to Governance Core and assign orchestration exclusively to Automation Core
summary: Re-issue of governance-core-rename-20261002 (lost to a concurrent amendment built on the same predecessor) combined with the orchestration assignment: governance-core handles governance business only (policy, architecture, change and result acceptance) and is forbidden from orchestration, scheduling, priority ordering and dependency sequencing; automation-core owns all orchestration (scheduling, priority ordering, dependency/state sequencing, dispatch assignment, synchronization). Pure responsibility/naming change: execution authority, permission-core and xingcheng-assistant duties and the decision-sovereign identity are unchanged.
origin: direct human-governor instruction 2026-10-02: rename the decision core to the governance core; give orchestration responsibility to the automation core; the governance core handles governance business only

changes.proposed: ROLES:GOVERNANCE_CORE=POLICY_AND_ACCEPTANCE;PERMISSION_CORE=IDENTITY_SCOPE_PERMISSION_DIRECTORY_SECURITY_ENFORCEMENT;RUNTIME_CORE=STARTUP_PROCESS_LIFECYCLE_GOVERNED_EXECUTION;AUTOMATION_CORE=AUTHORIZED_WORKFLOW_SCHEDULING_AND_SYNCHRONIZATION;XINGCHENG_ASSISTANT=INSPECTION_NOTIFICATION_USER_PERMISSION_PRESENTATION;XINGCHENG=NATIVE_MODEL_OWNED_CAPABILITIES;MODULE=BOUNDED_EXECUTION_WITHOUT_AUTHORITY;INFORMATION_LAYER=TYPED_CONTRACT_AND_STATUS. PIPELINE:decision intent>permission validation>registered dispatch>module execution>typed receipt>status projection. Each request activates exactly one role identity per participant;co-location never merges roles.

FINAL-ARCHITECTURE:governance-core,permission-core,runtime-core,automation-core and xingcheng-assistant are the five peer cores; Xingcheng is a separate native-model identity. RESPONSIBILITY:governance-core owns policy and acceptance decisions only (no orchestration);permission-core owns identity,scope,permission,directory and security enforcement;runtime-core owns startup,process lifecycle and governed execution;automation-core owns authorized workflow orchestration (scheduling,priority ordering,dependency/state sequencing),dispatch assignment and synchronization;xingcheng-assistant owns inspection,notification and user permission presentation. EXECUTION:C and Rust own deterministic runtime and lifecycle hot paths,C++ owns inference,audit,test execution and resource governance,CSharp owns application/API/workflow/test orchestration,FSharp owns business rules and high-correctness analysis,Go owns high-concurrency network/file/batch work. CONTRACT:all cross-core work uses registered versioned contracts,bounded execution,permission checks,receipts and fail-closed outcomes. Python has only the two request-scoped B4 responsibilities and is never a core host,coordinator or execution fallback.

AUTOMATIC-VALIDATION-CHAIN:governance-core validates assignment;permission-core automatically evaluates identity+action+target+scope+purpose+expiry+risk+grant/revocation+least-privilege and emits allow/deny authorization artifact;runtime-core validates artifact+executor+generation+resources+contract and dispatches; all stages are event-driven,typed,non-skippable and independently audited; any missing/stale/conflicting proof fails closed; normal operation requires no interactive confirmation

CURRENT:system-programming sovereign and sub-sovereign identities are abolished and historical only. OWNER:automation-core orchestrates authorized programming workflows;runtime-core owns governed execution;governance-core owns acceptance;permission-core enforces scope;registered modules perform work without authority.

SCOPE:every executable,service,worker,adapter,UI,test,maintenance and automation component. ASSIGNMENT:each capability maps to exactly one B162 core responsibility and one registered execution-module owner where execution exists. MAP:policy+acceptance>governance-core;identity+directory+permission+security-enforcement>permission-core;startup+process+lifecycle+execution>runtime-core;workflow+orchestration+priority-ordering+dependency-sequencing+synchronization+update+retention>automation-core;inspection+notification+user-permission-presentation>xingcheng-assistant;native-model+learning+programming-review>Xingcheng. MULTI-CAPABILITY:split independently assignable work into registered modules and express remaining relations as versioned dependency edges. CHANGE:owner change requires current Codex authority,affected graph,atomic cutover,one current owner and evidence.

SUCCESSOR:B114 completely supersedes A35,B61,A73 and A89 for current topology and startup interpretation. TOPOLOGY:the current roster is generated from active identity lifecycle and B162 and contains exactly governance-core,permission-core,runtime-core,automation-core and xingcheng-assistant as peer cores; XINGCHENG remains a separate native-model service identity outside the independent-tool roster. Historical sub-sovereign rows are lineage-only and excluded from every current roster,parent,route and ownership projection. STARTUP:MAIN_SYSTEM_DESKTOP_EXE>visible UI>SYS_GPTBRIDGE_START>information layer>runtime-core governed startup modules.

MAINTENANCE-UPDATE-INTEGRATION:the five current cores coordinate through registered modules under the single C50 governance engine. automation-core schedules update and backup modules;governance-core determines health acceptance and repair disposition;permission-core enforces scope and records directory/audit evidence;runtime-core performs governed process cutover or rollback;xingcheng-assistant independently audits alignment and notifies the user. Every module is single-owner,typed,fail-closed and non-authoritative. Historical maintenance sub-sovereign names are lineage-only under B162. GOVERNANCE-UNITY:C50 alone controls orchestration,dependency order,current-generation fencing,cancellation and receipt convergence;domain executors retain their registered scope and create no separate governance authority. Completion requires current permission,execution receipts and independent verification;missing or conflicting evidence isolates the affected scope and remains incomplete.

OWNER:automation-core. GOVERNANCE-ENGINE:one registered governance engine is the sole system-wide orchestration boundary for authorized governance workflows,including Git coordination and SQL governance;Git and SQL are domain planes of that engine and never independent schedulers,coordinators or governance authorities. RESPONSIBILITY:the engine receives current decision and permission artifacts,orders dependencies,applies generation fences,coordinates bounded domain executors,joins receipts,isolates conflicts and publishes one convergence result. AUTHORITY-SEPARATION:Git remains authority only for source and immutable repository history;PostgreSQL remains authority only for official mutable structured data and Codex state;the governance engine owns neither domain truth and cannot translate availability in one domain into authority over the other. ATOMICITY:a cross-domain change declares one correlation identity,one intended generation and one ordered transaction plan;Git commit publication,SQL migration or data mutation,verification and activation either converge to the same accepted generation or the affected change remains incomplete and fail-closed;no distributed transaction fiction or silent partial success is permitted. EXECUTION:registered Git and SQL modules perform bounded owner-language work and return typed receipts;runtime-core owns execution mechanics. FAILURE:a failure in one plane blocks only the dependent convergence path,preserves the last accepted state and evidence,and cannot corrupt or promote the other plane. SUCCESS:required Git,SQL,Codex,permission,runtime and audit identities,versions,hashes and receipts agree and independent verification passes. GOVERNANCE-UNITY:C50 controls the one governance orchestration engine for all registered system-wide workflows,including Git,SQL,Codex publication,permission-registry synchronization,release,maintenance,recovery and audit delivery. Every plane uses the same current Codex generation,task identity,correlation chain,permission proof,dependency ordering,cancellation and convergence contract. Governance-core retains decisions and acceptance;permission-core retains identity,scope and permission;runtime-core retains governed execution;automation-core retains orchestration;xingcheng-assistant retains independent read-side review. Domain executors cannot establish another control plane. A domain-specific operating loop remains bounded by its registered owner and cannot become a system-wide governance scheduler. Publication requires current authority-pointer,search,lifecycle,seal and mirror parity;stale or mixed generation blocks the affected activation.

GRANULARITY:isolate one unit or one module (selectable)|PURPOSE:failure boundary failure must not propagate to other units|EXECUTION:isolation+release+freeze executed by runtime core|ADJUDICATION:governance core when needed|AUDIT:full audit trail mandatory|SCOPE:on-demand only no permanent isolation without cause
